whatChanged.theChannel: The finalizer's own opt-in narrativeAcrossFields channel, one entry per field naming ONE fact id and ONE field, built from the census rows whose policy is 'narrative' and passed as narrativeAcrossFields: narrativeRows.map(...). The named fields are deliberately excluded from unwritableFields, because the narrative pass refuses a field classified unwritable by role, and deliberately absent from explicitMappings, because the ordinary pass SKIPS a named field entirely and never reaches a binding decision for it -- so the wrong fact cannot be written there first. The shared module resolves each fact from the same facts set every other write is resolved from, runs the same protect test on the caption AND on the field name, fits the value to that widget's own rectangle and refuses it WHOLE rather than truncating. No caller text can reach the page through it.
whatChanged.whyNoOtherChannelReachesTheseBoxes: MEASURED IN THIS CONTAINER AGAINST THE LIVE RULES. decideBinding tries the field NAME first and the printed LABEL only if the name matches nothing. 'Mailing Address.2' and 'Mailing Address1' both match /mailing\s*addr/ and resolve to participant.street_address; 'name.1', 'name.3' and 'name.4' all match /\bname\b/ and resolve to participant.full_legal_name.
